The War of Betony<br>
By Fav'te<br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br><br>
Could there be a better proof of the natural perversity of Bretons than their conduct before, during, and after what history will remember as the War of Betony? By the most depraved of motivations, the most despicable of tactics, and the most ungentlemanly of triumphs, the kingdom of Daggerfall changed the nature of warfare in the Iliac Bay and perhaps over all of Tamriel. In Sentinel, we call the recent carnage the Siege of Betony, but as the book of history is writ by the victors, let us speak instead of the War of Betony.<br><br>
Redguards by their nature are a modest and practical people. We are not phlegmatic like the High Elves, nor cowardly like the Wood Elves and Khajiiti. But what would infuriate and enrage the swaggering, vainglorious Nords and Bretons would not merit a shrug from a Redguard. Had any Breton kingdom possessed the little island of Betony, it would have been covetously guarded. Betony's trade would have been seriously restricted; its religion subjugated; its people bound by active and constant pledges and duties of vassalage. But Betony was not a Breton dominion. Betony was part of the Kingdom of Sentinel.<br><br>
King Lysandus -- may the Old Ones continue to torment his soul for his wickedness! -- saw the prosperous island which is closer to his land than to Sentinel, and his black heart turned to avarice. Through threats, lies, acts of piracy and, finally, invasion, Daggerfall illegally took possession of the Island of Betony. His court sorceress, the Lady Medora, his enchantress mother, and other experienced counselors were horrified by the brutality of his campaign and begged him to abandon his tyrannical act of war. Gradually, all dissenters were removed from court. None but the ignorant and the warmongers remained.<br><br>
Our late king Camaron tried to employ civil diplomacy with Daggerfall, but in the end, he made the former declaration of war. Daggerfall and Sentinel have fought many times in their two thousand years of coexistence, and Camaron knew the black magic and espionage the Bretons considered honest warfare. Never debasing the Sentinel character by duplicating the Breton villainy, Camaron knew best how to combat Lysandus. King Lysandus' knavish battle tactics were even more perfidious than his ancestors', and the war continue to rage until it began to involve more than Sentinel and Daggerfall.<br><br>
Lord Graddock, ruler of Reich Gradkeep, acted as conciliator between Sentinel and Daggerfall, and eventually convinced both monarchs to meet and make peace. The ill-fated Treaty of Gradkeep began civilly; the terms of peace were discussed, agreed on, and set to paper. The terms were excessively generous. Camaron had agreed to give up some of his rights to Betony in order to placate the madness of Lysandus and bring peace back to the Iliac Bay. It was not until King Camaron read the Treaty he was about to sign that he realized the outrageous perfidy of the Bretons: the Treaty had actually been purposefully miswritten by the Daggerfall scribe in a desperate and ignominious attempt to trick Camaron into signing a contract different from the one to which he had agreed. The castle of Reich Gradkeep erupted into bloodbath, and the war continued.<br><br>
The Battle of Cryngaine Field was the tragic ending of the senseless war of attrition. The Cryngaine Field is located in between the Yeorth Burrowland and the Ravennian Forest where the armies of Sentinel and Daggerfall respectively made camp after the massacre at Reich Gradkeep. As the battle began, Daggerfall proved that she had some foul daedric magical tricks left by blinding the Redguard army with a wall of mist. Lysandus did not have the opportunity to gloat over his cozenage for long, for the sure arm of a Sentinel archer struck him in the throat even through the thick, swirling fog. Lysandus' son, Gothryd, who had spent the battle in lugubrious relaxation, was crowned without ceremony, and thereupon demanded a duel with King Camaron. Camaron was many years Gothryd's senior, and though a superior warrior, was exhausted from the endless warfare the boy king had been spared. Nevertheless, as a point of honor, our king agreed to the duel. The new king of Daggerfall, by dirty trick and black magic, managed to backstab our king before the duel ever began. Thus, the victor of Cryngaine Field, and the War of Betony, was Daggerfall.<br><br>
Daggerfall's wickedness continued even after her inglorious victory. While the widow queen of Sentinel, Her Majesty Akorithi, mourned and tried to mend her shattered lands, Gothryd demanded the Princess of Sentinel as a hostage of war. To save her homeland, the Princess Aubk-i agreed to leave Sentinel and even marry the murderer of her father. But we true Redguards of Sentinel know where her love and honor lies. The Queen of Daggerfall is the Princess of Sentinel first and foremost.<br>

|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
The War of Betony<br>
By Vulper Newgate<br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br><br>
The history of the Iliac Bay, if told in its entirety, would horrify readers more than the most gruesome legend of the Underking. In comparison to the wars of the first and second era, our most recent appeal to arms, the War of Betony pales. The Siege of Orsinium lasted from 1E 950 until 1E 980 without a pause. A thousand years later, the Thrassian Plague coupled with the War of Righteousness slayed over half the population of the Iliac Bay. And yet, the War of Betony fascinates us, and not just because of its immediacy.<br><br>
Ironically, Lord Mogref of Betony was seeking peace when he asked for Daggerfall's protection on the Isle of Betony. The island had long been independent, but as the piracy in the Bay increased, Mogref truly realized Betony's vulnerability. King Lysandus agreed to be Betony's liege, on advice of many, including his archpriest of Kynareth, Lord Vanech. While Betony is a prosperous fishing island and well-placed strategically, the vassalage of Betony was primarily an act of charity. Lysandus knew that if someone did not help Betony, it would fall to the pirates, if not to someone worse.<br><br>
Unfortunately, King Camaron of Sentinel did not agree. Citing a two hundred year old contract, obliquely if not illegally written to suggest that Betony was a "traditional holding" of the Kingdom of Sentinel, Camaron declared war. The majority of his advisors, being warlords in a traditionally bellicose country, supported their king in this. The Chief Counselor, a woman called The Oracle, foresaw death and defeat in the war, but her wisdom was stifled and she was banished from court. Camaron should have listened to her.<br><br>
A few scrimmages of the War of Betony went to Sentinel, but the major battles were all won by Daggerfall. King Lysandus, his heir Prince Gothryd, and the general of the army Lord Bridwell were fine leaders and warriors as well, and the Battle of the Bluffs and the Siege of Craghold both went to Daggerfall.<br><br>
The war might have been won with one more victory, but for an unusual domestic incident in King Lysandus' court. The king's mother, the dowager queen Nulfaga, had been uneasy about the war since its beginning, but she now began to have visions of cataclysm. She saw the death of her beloved son should the war continue. Ebullient by his success, King Lysandus refused to listen to her fears until Nulfaga left court. Lysandus then realized how certain she was about his impending death. He began to actively negotiate a peace treaty with Sentinel, using the neutral lordship of Reich Gradkeep as facilitator.<br><br>
The Treaty of Reich Gradkeep was never to be. King Camaron was initially civil, as the losing side of a war is often civil, but when he realized that the proposed treaty would have included a formal declaration that the kingdoms of Sentinel and Daggerfall would share Betony, he flew into a rage. With no thought for the protocol of attacking a neutral peaceable lordship, Camaron order his army to riot through Reich Gradkeep. First the halls of the palace, and then the streets of the capitol ran red with blood. It was only with the support of the Daggerfall army that the chaos was brought under relative control. The Sentinel army fled to the Yeorth Burrowland, and the Daggerfall army chased them as far as the Ravennian Forest before making camp.<br><br>
One week later, after each had a chance to send for reinforcements and plan their strategies, the armies met in the field that separated them, the flowering meadowland called Cryngaine Field. In the heat of the clash, an unnatural fog spread over the field, blinding all combatants. When the mist finally lifted, King Lysandus' body was found, his throat pierced by an unmarked arrow.<br><br>
Daggerfall did not waste any time in mourning; young prince Gothryd, who had shown great bravery in battle and was very popular among the troops, was crowned King of Daggerfall just behind the battle lines, and he ordered the army onward. Perhaps it was the sight of the brave young warrior turned king appearing on the battlefield in full regalia that inspired the Daggerfall army, perhaps the battle would have turned regardless, Sentinel began to panic. King Gothryd met King Camaron before the Redguards had retreated, and the two monarchs fought. Both were excellent warriors, but Gothryd was a more skillful swordsman, and Camaron fell that day. Lord Oresme of Sentinel formally surrendered to Daggerfall, giving up all rights to Betony officially. He later committed suicide on the ship back to Sentinel.<br><br>
Peace was a difficult process for the cities and towns on both sides of the Iliac Bay. As part of the formal peace treaty, King Gothryd asked for the hand of Princess Aubk-i, only daughter of the late King Camaron and the Queen Regent Akorithi. The request was intended to restore friendship between the kingdoms, and it was partially successful though many in the royal court of Sentinel viewed the princess as more a prisoner of war than a bond to Daggerfall.<br><br>
The only surviving member of the ruling family of Reich Gradkeep was a sickly infant, so the councilors of state appealed to Lord Auberon Flyte, a cousin of Lord Graddock, to rule the lordship in regency. Lord Flyte accepted, and his strong, almost dictatorial style was just what Reich Gradkeep needed to restore order after the bloody Treaty of Reich Gradkeep. His subjects were grateful that when the infant heir died, they not only elevated his wife Doryanna and him from regents to rulers, they agreed to rename the lordship in his honor. Reich Gradkeep became Anticlere, named after his ancestral home.<br><br>
The horrors of the War of Betony still live on, even in Anticlere. Whether Daggerfall and Sentinel will be able to use the marriage of King Gothryd and Princess Aubk-i as a symbol of peace rather than discord is something that only the future can show.<br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="RIGHT"><br>
-- 14 Suns Dawn 3E 404<br>

|Name|    Wayrest, Jewel of the Bay [T_Note_WayrestJewelOfTheBayTR]
|Model|    m\Text_Parchment_02.nif
|Weight|    1.10
|Value|    90
|Scroll|    True
|Enchantment|    0
|Icon|    m\Tx_parchment_02.tga
|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Wayrest, Jewel of the Bay<br>
By Sathyr Longleat<br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br><br>
Wayrest is one of the most glorious cities of western Tamriel: sparkling in her contemporary beauty, lustrous by her past. She is prized above all cities in High Rock -- no other city has contributed, and continues to contribute so much to the culture of the Bretons. The spirits of her genius children continue to haunt the streets; you can see them in the gabled roofs, grand boulevards, aromatic marketplaces. The people of Wayrest have an instinctive appreciation of their past, but are not obsessed by it, as the people of Daggerfall seem to be. One feels that one is in a modern city when one visits Wayrest, but there is a magic in the air that could only come from thirty-two centuries of civilization.<br><br>
It is difficult for historians to declare a certain date for the foundation of Wayrest. A settlement of some variety had been existence where the Bjoulsae River feeds the Iliac Bay possibly since the 800th year of the First Era. The traders and fishermen of Wayrest were surrounded by hostile parties: the orc capitol Orsinium had grown like a poison weed to the north, and the Akaviri pirates and raiders crowded the islands to the west. There is no mystery to Wayrest's name. After the fighting most travellers had to endure passing through the eastern end of the Iliac Bay, the little fishing village on the Bjoulsae was a welcome rest.<br><br>
Nowhere in the much vaunted censuses of the Skyrim Occupation is Wayrest mentioned. In the Annals of Daggerfall, King Joile's letter to Gaiden Shinji of the Order of Diagna contains the following reference: "The orcs have been much plaguing the Wayresters and impeding traffic to the heart of the land." The date given for the letter was 1E 948.<br><br>
Wayrest only truly bloomed after the razing of Orsinium in 1E 980. The hard-working traders and merchants were instrumental in forming the Masconian Trade Way and thus reducing the pirate activity on the Bay. At this time, Wayrest occupied both banks of the Bjoulsae. A successful mercantile family, the Gardners, built a walled palace on the High Rock side of the river and, over time, allowed banks and other businesses within its walls. It was a Gardner, Farangel, who was proclaimed king when Wayrest accepted ambassadors from the Camorian Empire, and was granted the right to call itself a kingdom in the 1100th year of the 1st Era.<br><br>
Although Wayrest became a kingdom under the command of one family, the merchants continued to wield incredible power. Many economists have alleged that Wayrest's eternal wealth, despite all her hardships, comes from this rare relationship between the merchants and the crown. The Gardner Dynasty fell, followed by the Cumberland Dynasty, which was followed by the Horley Dynasty, and finally, in the Third Era, the Septim Dynasty. No citizen of another kingdom of comparable age can, with one hand, name all the families who have ever ruled. Never has a king of Wayrest been deposed by revolution or assassination. Except for those of the Septim family, every king of Wayrest can trace his line back to a merchant prince of Wayrest. The merchants and king respect one another, and this relationship strengthens both.<br><br>
One need only walk down the great boulevard of Wayrest to see physical proof of this unique alliance. Going north to south, Wayrest Boulevard suddenly divides, one half going west and the other going east. Both halfs end in identical squares: one at Castle Wayrest, the original palace of Aphren Gardner, and the other at Cumberland Square, where the oldest and wealthiest marketplace in Wayrest. The message here is clear: the king and the merchants are joined and equal.<br><br>
Wayrest has survived blights, droughts, plagues, piracy, invasions, and war with good humor and practicality. In 1E 2702, the entire population of the city was forced to move into the walled estate of the Gardners as protection against the pirates, Akaviri raiders, and Thrassian plague. A less resourceful community would have withered, but the Wayresters have survived to enrich Tamriel generation after generation.<br>

|Name|    A Blacksmith's Last Writ [T_Sc_BlacksmithsLastWritHR]
|Model|    m\text_scroll_03.nif
|Weight|    0.20
|Value|    1500
|Scroll|    True
|Skill|    Armorer
|Enchantment|    0
|Icon|    m\Tx_scroll_03.tga
|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
<br>
A Blacksmith's Last Writ<br>
<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Here in this writing, I, master smith Beross, born of the mountain-home betwixt the Northern Point and the mountain cities, bequeath my knowledge of the smithing of the material known as mithril. A process originally meant to be spoken and taught to an apprentice. But not any apprentice of any village in mountain nor seaside was able to learn my hammer-strike, nor my aptness with the forge.<br>
<br>
That is why, knowing that Archei will soon whisper my final words into my weakening ears, I will leave my knowledge to Kynaree's pious subjects. Thus a successor of equal ability might join me in forging those weapons that keep Sheor's servants in their unwelcome halls, as I might join my masters in Her cloud-palace.<br>
<br>
Forging mithril is a most challenging process to master. With improper technique, an object of mithril might be more fragile than glass and as brittle as the charcoal that was used to fire it. It requires special tools and a high quality iron that is both well malleable under heating, but rigid of construction when cool. The iron in the lower caves of the mountains has these qualities. The second major ingredient is what they call spellstones in common speech. These need to be of high purity, as any deformation in the crystal can weaken the integrity of the infusion. Crystal of highest purity can be obtained from those sites and thereunder where the druids of old performed their rites. The structure of the spellstone must ring bright and true, resonating in unison with the iron it will bond with. Failure shows the need to procure ingredients from better sources.<br>
<br>
Next, one needs to powder the spellstone, an intense and volatile process. One needs to crush it in a mortar with no surface imperfections, and grind it to a powder the consistency of fine sand. Magick might escape during this treatment, and one might keep it contained by hiring one proficient in the arcane arts, or by constructing a brass dome with mirrors of silver and glass. Next, one heats the metal close to white hot -- one needs a well-constructed kiln to do so -- and then one needs to work quickly. Brush the surface as to rid it of the influence of air and cold and add the spellstone to the metal, making sure to get even distribution and infusion. Fold the metal and add the spellstone to the metal eightfold in quick succession. Reheat after this process but once to near white, and draw the ply out to a desired shape to set its form. After cooling one can make the metal only red hot, to draw out the blade or plate, keeping the direction of one's previous blows. After satisfaction, quench in the salt-water of the ghostly sea, and sharpen or polish as necessary.<br>
<br>
These are but the fundamentals of smithing mithril. Often one needs to add patterns for the magick to flow into the desired direction, so as to strengthen the piece as a whole. This requires decades to master properly, as misdirected magicka impedes function, even though the blade might still keep its edge. This, however, cannot be conveyed in writing, and must be discovered by oneself to master it.<br>
<br>

<br>

Pale and feeble were the spirits of mortal men, their souls neither vivid nor strong.<br><br>

Great, and wise, and powerful are the Divines, and in their power they took pity on us.<br><br>
Led by the spirit Shezarr, they set about building the World as a house in which mortal souls could grow, by trial and sorrow.<br>
By trial and sorrow we are born, by trial and sorrow we die, and this was the idea of Shezarr.<br><br>
Many lesser spirits contributed to this great work, they became part of the World entirely. It was a long and difficult labor.<br>
Long and difficult was their labor, the labor of those we have forgotten.<br><br>

They who are pleased do not covet, they who covet are not pleased. Beware of spirits that are pleased yet covet.<br><br>

Not all were willing, not all are wont to pay the price. Let them flee, for their star-eyes are the prize of Shezarr.<br><br>

Forever diminished in the making, so freely did they give flesh, blood, and bone.<br><br>

The World their creation, bones speaking, blood washing, flesh feeding.<br><br>

To the place of death the Divines went, but not into death, into the world of the dead above us.<br><br>

Signs and mirages to guide and protect, in the sky, the earth, and the temples of Man.<br><br>

|Name|    Guide to Almas Thirr [T_Sc_GuideToAlmasThirrTR]
|Model|    M\text_scroll_01.nif
|Weight|    0.20
|Value|    3
|Scroll|    True
|Enchantment|    0
|Icon|    m\tx_scroll_01.dds
|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Almas Thirr<br><br>
<IMG SRC="tr\almasthirr_city_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Almas Thirr: pilgrim's rest, river's gate, and central jewel in the diadem of Veloth's Path. A city and a temple in one, Almas Thirr stands in tribute to the crossing of the mighty river Thirr by the faithful of the Velothi Exodus, founders of the nation of Morrowind. At the crossroads of the two great arteries of eastern commerce, Veloth's Path and the Thirr River, Almas Thirr has become a nexus of wealth and trade, and the city has expanded several times during its history to accomodate both the traders and priests who flock there.
<br>
River trade is more heavily regulated than road caravans. While caravans are permitted free passage through the city, ships large and small are stopped in the river lock for a cargo inspection. In order to avoid fines, confiscation of goods, or investigation by the Ordinators, travelers are advised to consult with Temple officials for the latest list of contraband before arriving in Almas Thirr by ship. Vessels intending to continue their journey upstream toward Narsis or downstream to Old Ebonheart must make a tribute to the Temple in the form of gold or trade goods.
<br>
Pilgrims on Veloth's Path are advised to rest for several days in Almas Thirr before continuing their westward journey to Othrenis and Almalexia. The Hostel of the Crossing provides free lodging for pilgrims. Most pilgrims will be familiar with the Bloodstone Pilgrimage, which is customarily hosted by the Hetman (leader) of the city's Velothi residents. This grueling undertaking terminates at the Bloodstone Shrine deep within the Monastery of St. Veloth. Faithful visitors may also wish to attend the frequent sermons at the Temple complex within the canton, or pray at the various shrines around the city. Of special interest is the Shrine to St. Veloth on the eastern bank, which is believed to be the one of the oldest shrines to that illustrious saint in all Morrowind. For those seeking quiet meditation, the balconies on the upper level of the canton provide an excellent vantage from which to contemplate the Mother Thirr. Travelers should be aware, however, that Temple officials have the prerogative use of these areas and may ask the meditating traveler to move to a location on the lower level.
<br>
Pilgrims seeking provisions for their onward journey need look no further than the canton, which contains all the services a pilgrim may need. For more worldly goods, visitors may visit Market Street on the city's west side, which hosts a plentitude of stalls and shops run by Velothi and outlanders alike. For those seeking protection on their journey, the Fighters Guild hosts warriors for hire, while the Mages Guild is home to some of the foremost enchanters in Morrowind. Travelers are advised to steer clear of the Docks district, as the constant transit of cargo and ongoing repair work to vessels in port may pose dangers to the incautious.
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="2" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Region Information
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
<br>
Almas Thirr sits at the heart of the bucolic Aanthirin region. Dotted with large plantations, small farms, and Velothi villages, and criss-crossed with good roads, the region around the Thirr River is very safe for even the most novice traveler. While not dangerous, hikers are advised to keep a safe distance from the graceful Velk which roam the region, as they are considered sacred to the Tribunal Temple and should not be disturbed. There are also a few ruins of old Indoril manors and even older strongholds of the ancient Chimer, both of which should be given a wide berth. Otherwise, the native fauna of Aanthirin should pose no threat to those who find themselves in the wilderness. Indeed, with welcoming settlements often a short journey away, there is little risk to a brisk hike into the country, and much reward in the region's idyllic vistas.
<br>
<IMG SRC="TR\oldebonheart_region_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="754"><br> <br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

|Name|    Guide to Bal Foyen [T_Sc_GuideToAndothrenTR]
|Model|    m\text_scroll_01.nif
|Weight|    0.20
|Value|    3
|Scroll|    True
|Enchantment|    0

|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Bal Foyen<br><br>
<IMG SRC="tr\bal_foyen_city_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
The great port city of Bal Foyen has been made wealthy by geography, but sanctified by the deeds of its patron goddess: the Queen of Mercy, Mother Morrowind, Lady Almalexia. Indeed, the proud residents of this jewel upon the Inner Sea often attribute the city's commercial prosperity to the blessing of Almalexia and her great deeds here. So long as the Temple stands upon her isle, it is said, Bal Foyen will never fall to ruin.

Tholer Andas, councilor of Great House Hlaalu, rules Bal Foyen from his grand estate overlooking the city. Beneath his lofty perch lies Warden Plaza, so named for Almalexia's war-aspect and in reverence for the peace that has endured under her rule. This part of Bal Foyen is home to the city's Fighters and Mages Guilds, as well as the local Council Manor of House Hlaalu. A traveler seeking rest may find it in the Dancing Cup Inn, while those in town to browse Bal Foyen's famous markets will find no shortage of bargains in Warden Plaza's shops. The renowned Port of Bal Foyen can be found just north of the plaza, its docks and warehouses buzzing perpetually with activity as goods depart and arrive from a score of foreign cities.

Western Bal Foyen -- what remains of its ancient core -- is today called the Old Town. Here, Dunmer live and work much as they have for a thousand years, producing goods no less fine than their expatriate competitors in Warden Plaza. The Old Town hosts many such businesses, as well as the city's Morag Tong hall. Visitors affiliated with House Hlaalu are advised to inquire at the Golden Moons Club, an establishment of fine repute and well-mannered staff. Less well-to-do arrivals to the Old Town would do well to watch their pocketbooks when staying at the Council Club. Adjacent to the Old Town is the Manor District, a Third Era neighborhood whose residents -- notables of the highest order -- live in luxurious fashion in resplendent manors, each with its own character. The Imperial Commission can also be found here, led by the redoubtable magistrate Janonia Melitus and Agronak gro-Dumag, commander of the local Imperial Legion garrison. A chapel dedicated to Mara offers services to the Imperial cult devotees and other visitors alike.

In the center of the city's districts lies the Temple Isle. When Almalexia defeated the armies of the invading Akaviri at the ancient village that once stood at this site, the ground first collapsed, then rose again in the center of the crater, forming the island that today hosts one of the most important temples of the Tribunal faith. The largest bridge on Temple Isle leads to the picturesque waterfalls that cascade down the city's cliffs, and to the famous Shrine of Almalexia's Fury.

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="2" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Region Information
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Bal Foyen lies in the Roth Roryn region, at the northwesternmost corner of Mournhold District. The crags and hills south and west of the city make overland travel difficult on foot, but silt striders pass over these obstacles with relative ease.

Roth Roryn

Roth Roryn is a vast, rocky region of pale red stone, hostile wildlife, and tough, hardy plants. Long considered a borderland between the Great Houses Redoran and Indoril, in recent centuries much of the Roryn has come to be dominated by the ascendant Great House Hlaalu. Although House Indoril has retreated east of the river Thirr and abandoned Roth Roryn, Redoran forces still garrison key outposts in this part of Resdayn, especially the approaches to the city of Veranis.

The constellation of small settlements to Bal Foyen's south and east are mostly agricultural in nature -- the plantation economy of Aanthirin extends even into these harsh badlands. Further west, though, the towns of Omaynis and Menaan scrape a hard living from the rocks themselves and from the trade of passing caravans. Across the Pryai River (which the Hlaalu have long sought to establish as the boundary of their control in the region), the great Monastery of Saint Felms stands astride the river's famous oxbow bend.

|Name|    Guide to Anvil [T_Sc_GuideToAnvilPC]
|Model|    M\text_scroll_01.nif
|Weight|    0.20
|Value|    3
|Scroll|    True
|Enchantment|    0
|Icon|    m\tx_scroll_01.dds
|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Anvil<br><br>
<IMG SRC="pc\pc_anvil_city_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
<br>
Anvil is the mightiest port city of the Abecean and the western gateway of Cyrodiil to the wider world. Its enormous harbor, bustling streets, and gleaming temples have made Anvil and its kingdom a destination for sailors, merchants, and pilgrims alike for centuries.
<br>
Any educated reader will surely be familiar with Anvil's historic role in naval history, as home port to both the All Flags Navy of the First Era and the fleets of Tiber Septim in the late Second Era. Today the city retains this proud distinction as host to Fort Telodrach, home of the Empire's distinguished West Navy.
<br>
Anvil services trade from half a hundred ports in Tamriel and beyond. Civilian vessels dock at the Port Quarter, the sprawling complex of quays and wharfs which stretches across much of the city's western edge. Saint Bendu Square, the heart of the Port Quarter, is easily spotted by the statue of Bendu Olo, which lies just inland from the piers. The tower headquarters of the Abecean Trading Company are found here, along with the city's famous Shipworks and the Chapel of the Tranquil Sky. Travelers seeking accommodation in the Port Quarter might seek out the Sailor's Fluke -- but keep a close eye on your purse.
<br>
Further inland from the Port Quarter lies Little Arenthia, Anvil's most working-class neighborhood. Best known for its Wood Elf community, Little Arenthia is also home to the city bathhouse, which is free and open to all. The Anchor's Rest provides modest, but comfortable accommodations to visitors here for a price, while the doors of the Hostel of Saint Rosunius are always open to the indigent.
<br>
Most of central Anvil is called the Marina. Here, the terminus of the mighty Gold Road is crowded with guild halls, Imperial Societies, temples, art galleries, and fine merchant shops. Members of the Fighters and Mages Guilds will find comrades in this part of the city, and services to meet one's every need. Travelers are encouraged to visit the Census and Excise offices in the Marina District, and to check in at the Harbormaster's office if arriving by sea. There are two temples in this part of the city: the Temple of the First Breath, just inside the walls, and the Chapel of Solemn Echoes, just outside them. The editors recommend the All Flags Inn, the oldest inn in Anvil, for travelers seeking a stay in the Marina. Caravaners may also find accommodations at the Caravan Stop.
<br>
Anvil's most glamorous -- and most famous -- neighborhood is doubtlessly the Garden Quarter. This part of Anvil is a gleaming boulevard, stretching from the towering Bazaar of the Abecean past the finest shops and the most luxurious manors to the steps of the immense Temple of Dibella Estetica, the largest in the world dedicated to the Goddess of Beauty. Here lies also Anvil's most upscale hotel: the Abecette, renowned the world over for its gambling halls, elegant rooms, and fighting pits. Travelers with deep pockets may wish to withdraw funds from the local branch of the Briricca Private Bank or trade stocks at the Trident Exchange.
<br>
<IMG SRC="pc\pc_anvil_bazaar_ad.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="189"><br><br><DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Looming above the entire city is Goldstone, the mighty castle of Her Serene Highness the Queen of Anvil. Goldstone's public audience halls are comfortable and luxuriant, but travelers are warned to follow the law in Anvil, lest they find themselves instead in the castle's vast and labyrinthine depths.
<br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="2" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Region Information
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><br>
<IMG SRC="pc\pc_anvil_region_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="189"><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
The city of Anvil sits on a peninsula, and is surrounded by water on three sides. To the west lies the Abecean Sea, from which the city reaps its bounty in trade and fish. To the south, the mouth of the River Strid forms the western edge of Cyrodiil's border with Valenwood Province. Along Anvil's northern walls, the Naharine River runs parallel to the Strid.
<br>
Strident Coast
<br>
The Strident Coast that surrounds Anvil is a fertile, pleasant land of low rolling hills and gentle fields. Some of the most productive agricultural lands in Colovia may be found here, and the kingdom's orchards, farms, and ranches waste none of its potential. Besides the ancient Ayleid ruin Garlas Agea and the great ridge upon which it sits, there are few impassable features to impede travel in any direction.
<br>
Outside Anvil proper, the Strident Coast is not all farmland and field. The trade-town of Brina Cross on the Gold Road serves as the Kingdom's gateway to interior Colovia. The smaller villages of Hal Sadek, Marav, and Thresvy are inhabited by more rural folk. These lands are old, and long-inhabited. A careful traveler may find their bearings by the old Reman coastal fortresses of Olomachus and Thraswatch, now crumbling into dust alongside the far older Ayleid citadel called Lindasael.
<br>
Dasek Marsh
<br>
Much of Colovia's southern border is the Dasek Marsh, a dense, tropical region whose green foliage chokes the banks of the Strid River. The Dasek Marsh is less settled than the Strident Coast, a fact which enterprising smugglers from Valenwood and Cyrodiil alike have long used to their advantage. The ancient Reman fortress of Strand is the main landmark in Dasek Marsh's westernmost reaches.
<br>
The only Dasek Marsh settlement in the Kingdom of Anvil is Archad, a river-port inhabited by traders and fisherfolk.
<br>
Abecean Sea and Stirk Isle
<br>
The Kingdom of Anvil is unique among the kingdoms of Colovia in that it governs not just a swathe of land, but a swathe of sea as well. It is in these myriad isles of the eastern Abecean Sea, and the trade-lanes between them, that the Kingdom of Anvil leverages its strength as an economic power. The so-called Golden Triangle trade circuit between Anvil, Rihad, and Stros M'Kai lies mostly in Anvil waters, with Stirk Isle in the center. These seas are among the most heavily traveled in the known world, and the seabed is said to be a treasure trove of lost wrecks, coral reefs, and caves of great natural beauty. Travelers should nevertheless take care, for sailors tell of darker, more dangerous things in these seas as well.
<br>
The isle of Stirk is the jewel of the Abecean, a shining tropical paradise surrounded by cerulean waves. Its only settlement, the town of Charach, is a cultural crossroads between Colovian, Redguard, and High Elven culture best known for its famous Temple of the West Wind.
<br>

|Name|    Guide to Dragonstar [T_Sc_GuideToDragonstarSHOTN]
|Model|    M\text_scroll_01.nif
|Weight|    0.20
|Value|    3
|Scroll|    True
|Enchantment|    0
|Icon|    m\tx_scroll_01.dds
|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Dragonstar<br><br>
<IMG SRC="sky\dragonstar_city_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Since the conclusion of the War of the Bend'r-Mahk some thirty years ago, Dragonstar has been a divided city. Dragonstar East is the westernmost holding of the Nordic Kingdom of the Reach, ruled in the name of King Barda of Markarth Side by Jarl Jona of clan Fire-Hand. The western city, meanwhile, remains under the control of Redguard Crowns, the last remnant of Hammerfell's northern Karthwasten Tomba. During the crises of the Imperial Simulacrum, Legion forces hastily erected a wall between the city's occupied areas to put a stop to the brutal fighting within the city. The wall stands to this day, and a careful traveler will take care when crossing.
<br>
Jarl Jona "the Ansei-Ender" rules her holdings from Castle Dragonstar in the eastern city. Dragonstar East is also home to the city's Arena and its Fighters Guild, though the latter has been defunct since the war. Only one establishment, the Shadowkey Tavern, offers rooms in the east, but travelers seeking only gossip and refreshments might seek out Ildgar's Alehouse. Much of Dragonstar East was heavily damaged during the war, and some areas have not been reconstructed.
<br>
The western half of the city, ruled by Prince Alak'tol since his narrow childhood escape from his former seat at Karthwasten, suffered less damage during the war. Dragonstar West is home to the city's Grand Bazaar, as well as its Mages Guild chapter. Travelers seeking accommodations have more options in the western city; both the Dragon Fountain Inn and Nukra-Tikil Tavern offer beds for rent.
<br>
Visitors to Dragonstar should be aware that travel across the Imperial-maintained dividing wall is heavily restricted. Additional precautions should be taken to ensure personal safety; politically-driven violence is common on both sides of the wall.
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="2" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Region Information
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><br>
<IMG SRC="sky\dragonstar_region_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Dragonstar lies in the upper reaches of the Druadach Highlands, where it commands the Tro-Tuktura canyon pass to Hammerfell. Outside the eastern walls sits Taurus Hall, headquarters of the Imperial Legion in the Highlands.
<br>
Druadach Highlands
<br>
The Druadach Highlands are a barren, windy region, and the ancestral homeland of the Reach's native population. One such village of Reach-folk, called Mairager, lies just east of Dragonstar. Members of the Alovach tribe here often trade with the city, and some of its number choose to live in Dragonstar permanently. Three mesas enclose the city on its other three sides: Coimeaden Mesa to the north, Darvacriag Mesa to the west, and Briag Cnoss to the south. Coimeaden is the most desolate of the three, hosting only a pair of ancient Direnni Elf ruins, Angturiel and Celera. Darvacriag is controlled by the Taliesinn tribe of Reach-folk, who live both in settlements of their own making and in the remains of the great Direnni citadel Vars Tharrnil. Friendly Reachmen of the Pachkanan tribe control Briag Cnoss. The mesa once hosted several Redguard villages, though all were destroyed by the war.
<br>
Western Vorndgad Forest
<br>
The vast Vorndgad Forest covers the terrain east of Dragonstar and the Druadach Highlands. This side of Karthgad, the most notable landmark is the forbidding ancient Nord fortress Vastangar. The ruined Direnni outpost Amrothal can also be found far to the north, on a hill overlooking farmland on the edges of the barren Falkheim region.
<br>

|Name|    Guide to Firewatch [T_Sc_GuideToFirewatchTR]

|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Firewatch<br><br>
<IMG SRC="tr\firewatch_city_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Firewatch, capital of Telvannis District, is a shining beacon of Empire on the edge of the hostile lands of the interior far northeast. Though its surroundings are bleak, ashen, and dangerous, within the walls of Firewatch a traveler may forget that they are not in one of the pleasant cities of the west. Despite their many hardships and privations in the crises of recent decades, the residents of Firewatch retain a hardy pride for their fine city at the edge of the world.

In recent years, Firewatch has become a center of commerce and academic thought, but the city retains a martial character from its origins as a crude coast fortress in the days of the Armistice. Duchess Perulia Jandacia rules from Ember Keep, her fortified palace in the Old Fortress, which also hosts the local offices of the Imperial Commission. Fort Dustmoth, headquarters of the storied Dustmoth Legion, stands just across the courtyard. From miles away, a traveler may behold Firewatch's most recognizable landmark, the Drakelight Beacon, which remains the tallest Imperial structure in the Eastern Provinces even a century after its construction.

Firewatch's famously large harbor, built to accommodate the grand host of the doomed Far East Fleet's northerly contingent, today has embraced its role as a commercial hub for northeastern Tamriel. Its deep berths host merchant vessels from as far afield as Bal Foyen, Winterhold, and Port Mare, bringing fine goods from the Sea of Ghosts and the Padomaic Ocean. The East Empire Company's district headquarters are found here, ever industrious in its commitment to bring fine eastern goods to the good people of the west. Travelers arriving in Firewatch should declare any imports to the Census and Excise Office, which sits adjacent to the regional headquarters of the Inner Sea Fleet.

Readers are advised to bypass Uriel's Quarter, a neighborhood of ill repute hosting an infestation of pickpockets and gamblers whose proclivities shame the memory of the beloved War-Emperor. The Hanging Noose tavern, the epicenter of this vice, should be avoided in particular. Instead, the wise traveler should make for the Market Quarter, where respectable merchants offer bargains on fine goods from Firewatch's many sister ports. The Queen's Cutlass, the city's best inn, can be found here; there is no finer accommodation in all the northeast. Those inclined towards mercenary work may seek it out at the Fighters Guild near the north gate.

Vaynth Quarter, Firewatch's newest district, is the epicenter of its modern reinvention as a renowned center of learning. The College of Firewatch, one of the finest educational institutions in the Eastern Provinces, permits visitors to occasionally observe lectures by its highly qualified faculty. The district branch of the Briricca Private Bank can be found here, alongside the Mages Guild and a number of high-class merchants.

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="2" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Region Information
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Firewatch is surrounded on three sides by the badlands of northern Telvannis District, the most hostile of Morrowind's mainland Districts. Consequently, the city's outlook has traditionally been towards the sea, and to this day there are few good roads out into the backcountry.

Dagon Urul

The Dagon Urul wasteland is an ashen expanse of hills and cliffs that sprawls across the northwestern third of Telvannis. Mount Sarrunabi, a volcano of frightful size dwarfed only by its counterpart on Vvardenfell, lies at the region's center, just northeast of Firewatch. It is often difficult to tell, when the ash storms rage across the region, whether the ash and dust in the air has come from Red Mountain, Mount Sarrunabi, or both at once. Indeed, Dagon Urul is no place for the faint of heart.

The region is known for its prominent Dwarf ruins, most notably Bthalag-Zturamz, which perches on a coastal promontory just south of Firewatch's walls. This region's ruins, however, are simply too dangerous to recommend to sightseers -- even their exteriors are often haunted by the still-crawling automata of the ancient Dwarves. Indeed, there is little to recommend to a civilian traveler beyond Firewatch's walls at all. The only Imperial outposts in these benighted lands were scoured away by the chaos of the Simulacrum, and an unwary tourist is likely to be set upon by wild animals or taken captive by hostile Dark Elves.

|Name|    Guide to Hlerynhul [T_Sc_GuideToHlerynhulTR]

|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Hlerynhul<br><br>
<IMG SRC="tr\hlerynhul_city_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Seat of the respected Hleryn Clan of House Hlaalu, Hlerynhul is a burgeoning trade city strategically located where the Kanit joins the Thirr on the banks of Lake Coronati. From Hlerynhul's humble beginnings as a ferry crossing (known as Hleryn Ferry for most of its history), the Hleryn Clan have patiently reinvested their wealth into their city and its citizens; it is now the most prosperous settlement in the Coronati region. The city's most recent public work, its inimitable bridge which soars across the Kanit-Thirr confluence was the brainchild of House Hlaalu Councillor Arven Hleryn, ancestor of current governor, Ivul Hleryn; it was built to service the road trade between the metropolis of Narsis and House Hlaalu's holdings downstream. This wise investment will pay dividends for the Hleryn Clan, and promises more growth in the future, as the city now can toll traders taking the land route.

Forward-looking and cosmopolitan, Hlerynhul boasts both a temple to the Tribunal and an Imperial Cult chapel dedicated to the veneration of Dibella. The construction of the chapel was spearheaded by the governor Ivul Hleryn, not because he venerates the Nine Divines himself, but because he professes a vision for a future of Morrowind where individuals of any race or creed can intermingle and cooperate for the mutual benefit of all. Imperial citizens, no matter their place of birth, can feel secure within Hlerynhul's walls, knowing they are protected by the Tribunal, the Nine Divines, and the Hleryn Clan alike.

The city of Hlerynhul is also dually protected by both Hlaalu House guards, supplied by the Hleryn Clan, and the Imperial Legion, based out of Tiger Hall on the Kanit's north bank. These noble public servants work in concert to enforce Hlaalu House law. Tiger Hall provides a practical staging-point for the Legion's policing operations in the Othreleth Woods, where lawless brigands and goblin clans continue to lurk and harass the dutiful Imperial taxpayer. It is only through cooperation between Imperial and House Hlaalu authorities that these lawless elements can be subdued; nowhere is this cooperation better shown than in the Imperial Legion's operation of Tiger Hall.
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="2" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Region Information<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><IMG SRC="tr\hlerynhul_region_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
The Coronati Basin is a fertile region which surrounds Lake Coronati and the middle bends of the Thirr River. It is largely serene, and dotted with many small holdings where diligent Velothi and immigrant outlanders alike till the soil. Travelers through the region should however be warned that its swamps, renowned for their towering fungal mangroves, can conceal various dangers. Trolls are known to flourish in these dank conditions, while the ruins of unkinder times may be only partially subsumed by the muck. The wise tourist would stick to the roads, and watch his step when striking out cross country.

Upstream on the Kanit River, the Othreleth Woods are not recommended for casual travelers. While bastions of civilization exist, and roads are patrolled by House Hlaalu and Imperial Legion forces alike, the dense woods are also a favored hiding-place for outlaws and monsters. A brave traveler, well-armed and accompanied by stalwart companions, may, however, take delight in the region's colorful vistas, and bounty of potent alchemical ingredients.<br>

|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Karthwasten<br><br>
<IMG SRC="sky\karthwasten_city_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Karthwasten is the largest city in the Reach, a vibrant cultural meeting-place, and a historic center of trade. Though it suffered damage in the War of the Bend'r-Mahk, today Karthwasten remains a wealthy and prosperous center of culture and commerce.
<br>
Jarl Jona of the Fire-Hand clan legally rules Karthwasten from her seat at Dragonstar, but in practice the city is controlled by her Thane, Fomir. Fomir - called "the Voiceful" - has ruled Karthwasten from the Red Palace with King Barda's support since the tense resolution to the Second Siege of Karthwasten.
<br>
Besides the grandiose Red Palace, Karthwasten hosts a number of other locations of note. The Dancing Saber and the Ruby Drake Inns offer warm beds to travelers, and some of the Reach's finest wares can be purchased the Bazaar in the center of the city. A Fighters Guild chapter can be found adjacent to the farms inside the walls, and the Guild of Mages has a hall near the north gates.
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="2" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Region Information
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><br>
<IMG SRC="sky\karthwasten_region_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="189"><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
From its plateau seat, Karthwasten is able to control both forks of the upper Karth River, the whole of Lorchwuir Heath, and a sizeable portion of the Vorndgad Forest.
<br>
Lorchwuir Heath
<br>
The rolling hills and low plateaus of the Lorchwuir Heath are the most developed part of the southern Reach, and have for centuries been a crossroads of trade and culture. Nords, Bretons, High Elves, Redguards, Reachmen, and Orcs have all ruled this part of Tamriel at one point or another, and relics of all these peoples may be found by those with a keen eye. Though banditry is minimal here, thanks to Karthwasten's dominating presence, travelers should take care not to stray too far from the roads, as there are still places where the law of Thane Fomir does not reach.
<br>
Druadach Highlands
<br>
Two native Reachmen settlements can be found to the west, on the summit of the plateau called Briag Cnoss. The larger, called Haimtir, sits amidst the ruins of the more sizeable town of the same name destroyed during the war. Criaglorc, a hostile camp of Reach-folk in the shadow of the immense ruined Direnni citadel Mirilstern, sits between Haimtir and Karthwasten. South of Briag Cnoss lies the border outpost of Vorngyd's Stand, named for the late King of the Reach whose heroic command of the pass sealed a notable victory of Nord forces in during the latter days of the war.
<br>
Vorndgad Forest
<br>
The Vorndgad Forest is a densely timbered swathe of land north of Karthwasten that stands in stark contrast to the breezy, open terrain of the Lorchwuir Heath and the Druadach Highlands plateaus. These woods are old; enterprising travelers often stumble across ruins of empires long lost amidst the rolling hills and granite cliffs. Chief among these in the south is the striking Nordic fortress ruin Vornberg, now crumbling into dust as the centuries roll past. Far to the east, across the eastern fork of the Karth, sits a hilltop settlement of the Reachman Hunnath tribe called Cairac.
<br>
Karthgad
<br>
The only settlement of note in the Vorndgad Forest, Karthgad is the seat of the Bear Clan, an old and proud Nordic clan who boasts of holding the line against Redguard incursions down the Karth in the days before the War. Thane Gorvrda rules Karthgad in King Barda's name.
<br>
Sundered Hills
<br>
East of the Karth River's eastern fork and over the pines of the Vorndgad Forest lie the gravelly slopes of the Sundered Hills. Straddling the borderlands between the Reach, White Hold, and Falkreath Hold, the region's treacherous terrain and foggy conditions have doomed many an army. Atop one such hill sits the ruined Remanite fortress Herax, constructed during the Hestran conquest of the Reach in the First Era.
<br>
Beorinhal
<br>
The Rock of the Reach, the Granite Hall, Beorinhal is the oldest Nordic settlement in the entire Reach. Jarl Horir, brother to the late King Vorngyd, rules here, and serves as his nephew Barda's loyal right hand in military matters. Now that the city no longer guards the border with Hammerfell, and the region's economic center has shifted to Karthwasten, Beorinhal's population has dwindled somewhat. It remains an important center of power in the south, however.
<br>

|Name|    Guide to Narsis District [T_Sc_GuideToNarsisDistrictTR]

|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
GUIDE TO NARSIS DISTRICT<br>
An overview of the district of Narsis.<br>
<br>
<IMG SRC="tr\narsis_district_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
Morrowind is the northeasternmost province of the Tamrielic Empire, bordered on the north and east by the Sea of Ghosts, on the west by Skyrim, on the southwest by Cyrodiil (also known as the Imperial Province), and on the south by Black Marsh (also known as Argonia). Narsis District encompasses the southwestern corner of the province, a stretch of land bounded by the Velothi Mountains and the border to Cyrodiil to the west, the desert canyons of Shipal-Shin and the border to Black Marsh to the south, the Thirr River basin to the east, and the dusty Armun Ashlands to the north.<br>
<br>
Narsis District is the heart of House Hlaalu trade; its cities, including Narsis, Kragenmoor, Andrethis, and Hlerynhul, are heavily populated and have had a history of mingling with nations of men for centuries. The many towns in the interior of the district are decently populated centers of agriculture and manufacturing, while the canyons to the south surrounding the city of Narsis are thinly populated, hosting tribal bandits and natural predators.<br>
Narsis District has four major geographic regions, each with their own distinctive plants and terrain features. These geographic regions are called: the Coronati Basin, the Othreleth Woods, Shipal-Shin, and the Velothi Mountains.<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><br>
CORONATI BASIN<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
<br>
The Coronati Basin is a fertile region centered on Lake Coronati, which lies at the intersection of the great Thirr River and one of its main tributaries, the Kanit River. The area includes Hlerynhul, Othmura, Ald Iuval, Ald Marak, and Sadrathim, as well as the lake itself and the streams, bogs, and mangroves that encircle it. The city of Hlerynhul is fairly densely populated, with many plantations, trade towns, and fishing villages surrounding it. The climate is humid around the water and mangroves, with a fair amount of rainfall, but is more arid further away from the shoreline.<br>
<br>
Hlerynhul is the seat of Hlaalu Councilor Ivul Hleryn, who has made his fortune by taxing and regulating trade across the Kanit and Thirr Rivers. The city is accessible mainly by boat, and hosts many services and points of interest, including the Chapel of Dibella.<br>
<br>
Othmura is a small trade town on the Thirr River route from Narsis to Old Ebonheart or Bal Foyen.<br>
<br>
Ald Iuval, along with its complement on the other side of the Thirr River, Ald Marak, are the remnants of the Waters March; they are the two standing Redoran towns in Narsis District.<br>
<br>
Sadrathim is a tiny fishing village, hosting the Chapel of Stendarr. It is the ancestral home of Clan Sadras of House Hlaalu.<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><br>
OTHRELETH WOODS<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
<br>
The Othreleth Woods are dense woods of tall mushrooms surrounding the Kanit River, north of the desert canyons of Shipal-Shin and south of the dusty Armun Ashlands. The city of Kragenmoor lies on its western border, with Andrethis in the heart of the region. The villages of Reluran, Hla Rud, Ilanaam, Fervinthil, and Narun lie along the river Kanit, with Narusa Winery along Veloth's Path. Tiny farms and mines abound in the Othreleth Woods, as well as ruined Redoran and Reman Empire fortifications from the past. The woods experience high humidity and heavy rainfall on average.<br>
<br>
Kragenmoor is a densely populated city near Shadowgate Pass at the end of the Blue Road. Its population is highly diverse due to its proximity to Cyrodiil, and the city's rule is contested between Hlaalu Councilors Llaasa Indarys and Edayn Sadras. Kragenmoor has seen a recent boom in trade from Nibenay, rivaling Narsis in economic prosperity.<br>
<br>
Andrethis lies at the heart of the Hlaalu logging and shipbuilding industries; it hosts the residence of Councilor Rhetixia Cheynoslin. Roads lead northwest to Kragenmoor, and southeast to Hlerynhul and Narsis.<br>
<br>
Reluran, Hla Rud, Ilanaam, Fervinthil, and Narun are small villages scattered through the Othreleth Woods with access to the Kanit River.<br>
<br>
Narusa Winery, just off the road from Veloth's Path, is home to Hlaalu Councilor Falena Narusa, one of the largest producers of shein and greef in Morrowind.<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><br>
SHIPAL-SHIN<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
<br>
The red canyons of Shipal-Shin rise up far to the south adjoining the Valus Mountains, forming a natural border both with Cyrodiil and Black Marsh. Isolated Hlaalu settlements can be found in the canyons, with inhabitants tilling the red soil and tending the sparse foliage. The most prominent city of Shipal-Shin is Narsis, the capital of House Hlaalu, grown grand and decadent from the wealth gained by supplying the Empire's failing Black Marsh settlements. Other towns in the region include Shipal-Sharai and Salvelis, with Hlaalu plantations, Imperial border forts, and Shinathi camps dotting the canyons. Shipal-Shin is mostly dry and dusty, with some rainfall around the source of the river Thirr.<br>
<br>
Narsis is the second most populous city in Morrowind after Almalexia, and perhaps the most wealthy. Ruled by Grandmaster Athires Hlaalu, the city hosts district headquarters of most Imperial Guilds and native factions, including the Hlaalu Council Company and the Measurehall, both centers of Hlaalu finance and administration. The Imperial Proconsul to Morrowind, Galvus Pottreid, also keeps a palace in the city, and Duke Fethas Hlaalu resides in Riverkeep, on the outskirts alongside major plantations of Clans Dren and Vedas.<br>
<br>
Shipal-Sharai is a caravan town, fueled by traders on the Purple Road from Mir Corrup to Narsis, but it has been experiencing hardships due to the failure of the local sapphire mine.<br>
<br>
Salvelis is a small village in the northwesternmost reaches of Shipal-Shin, close to the southern Velothi Mountains.<br>
<br>
Shipal Shin is home to the Shinathi, tribal brigands who make a living in the highlands extorting travelers and herding insects. The Gan-Ettu, Nasar, Ussiran, Hunza, Kuzali, and Ayahali tribes all have permanent camps around the region.<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><br>
VELOTHI MOUNTAINS<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
<br>
Narsis District also includes the southern region of the Velothi Mountains, the towering bulwark that separates Morrowind from the provinces of Cyrodiil and Skyrim. Aside from some small farms on the outskirts of Kragenmoor, the only settlement in the region is the border fort of Shadowgate Pass. The southern Velothi Mountains are cold and stark compared to the heat and humidity of most of Narsis District, with occasional snowfall.<br>

|Name|    Guide to Narsis [T_Sc_GuideToNarsisTR]
|Model|    M\text_scroll_01.nif

|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Narsis<br><br>
<IMG SRC="tr\narsis_city_map_00.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><IMG SRC="tr\narsis_city_map_01.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="189"><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Narsis is the largest city on Morrowind's mainland after Almalexia, and is the capital city of House Hlaalu. It is the province's financial capital, with many outlander residents and visitors who come to conduct business with House Hlaalu. Hundreds of tourists are seen passing through the Grand Bazaar every day to purchase exotic Dunmeri wares, and locals often visit to purchase international merchandise. Most outlander business is conducted in the Foreign Quarter, with most native commoners living in the skyscrapers of St. Veloth Quarter. The Waterfront processes shipments going to and from the city, and the Market Quarter is where the majority of the city's shops are located. The Old Quarter and Council Quarter house the wealthiest citizens of Narsis and contain the main residences of Clan Hlaalu, as well as the Grand Council Hall and other official House locations. Surrounding the city are various manors and plantations, as well as the Narsis District Duke's residence in Riverkeep.<br>
<br>
Narsis' six districts are centered on the Council Quarter mesa, with the Market Quarter below to the northwest, St. Veloth Quarter to the north, the Waterfront to the east, and the Old and Foreign Quarters to the south. Across the river, Riverkeep is south, Old Dren Plantation is southeast, and Vedas Plantation is east.<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
Market Quarter<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">The Market Quarter, Narsis' newest district, is located on the Purple Road to the northwest. Originally it was simply an informal day-market for caravaners and local farmers to gather; the Market Quarter grew into a full district post-Armistice as traders and travelers, who couldn't find room in the Foreign Quarter, built inns and houses to accommodate themselves. The population is a mix of Dunmer natives and outlanders. Among the important locations are the Mesa Exchange, the province's newest and only stock exchange, the multi-level Grand Bazaar, the Farmers and Laborers Hall, and the lavish manor of the Sixth Family of Clan Hlaalu. <br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
St. Veloth Quarter<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">Located directly north of the Council Quarter, St. Veloth Quarter (sometimes called St. Veloth's Square or simply St. Veloth's) is home to Narsis' working class population. In the First Era, the residents of Narsis' third-oldest district farmed the land of what is now the Market Quarter and Foreign Quarter or worked as boatmen plying the river. As House Hlaalu moved its people out into the former Waters March over the course of the Second Era, the population of St. Veloth's Square became poorer, a trend that continues into the current era. Important locations in this Quarter include the two giant apartment towers named the Velothi Tower and Brevur Heights. There is also the Morag Tong Hall and the guildhalls of the Miners and Tanners, the Tailors and Dyers, and the Cat Catchers. <br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
Waterfront<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">The Waterfront is Narsis' eastern district, built against the Council Quarter's cliffs at great expense by House Hlaalu. The Waterfront houses several local merchant companies, including the East Empire Company. The famous "Merchant-Prince of Narsis", Dravos Turil, owns a large shop in the Waterfront, and the Fortuna casino functions as the center of the city's red-light district. Other important locations include the Sailors and Shipbuilders Hall and the large manor of the Seventh Family of Clan Hlaalu.<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
Old Quarter<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">The Old Quarter is, as the name suggests, the oldest continuously inhabited part of the city and is the smallest district in area. It is essentially a road located between the Council and Foreign Quarters. Much of the old nobility lives here, as well as some of the middle-class Dunmer who work directly for House Hlaalu. The First Family of House Hlaalu live in the oldest building in the city, a manor facing the entrance to the Council Quarter.<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
Council Quarter<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">The Council Quarter is the center of governance for House Hlaalu, and contains the luxurious palace of the Second Family of Clan Hlaalu. This palace is the home of the Grandmaster of House Hlaalu, High Hlaalu Athires. Among other important locations are the Measurehall, which is the center of House business in the province, as well as the Imperial Consulate, the Eight-Bones Temple and the Arena.<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
Foreign Quarter<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">The Foreign Quarter is the southernmost district of Narsis. Before the Armistice, outlander merchants were only permitted to trade on the south flat, which was farmland tended by slaves that regularly flooded when the river swelled. Merchants profited so much from doing business directly in Narsis that a shack town was formed on the flat, becoming the original Foreign Quarter. Over the millenia it was gradually built into a part of the city proper. This district houses the Mages Guild, Fighters Guild, the Chapel of Zenithar, and the Narsis District's headquarters for the Imperial Legion, Heron Hall. The Foreign Quarter also holds the entrance to the expansive Narsis Catacombs.<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
Transportation<br>
<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><IMG SRC="tr\narsis_region_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="189"><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">Foot bridges connect the main peninsula to the Purple Road in the southwest and to the Market Quarter in the northwest. Good roads branch from the Purple Road leading north to the Coronati Basin and south around the Thirr River to Narsis' outskirts, which include the Duke's palace at Riverkeep, Old Dren Plantation and Vedas Plantation. The Purple Road itself leads west through Shipal-Sharai and Septim's Gate Pass to reach Cyrodiil. Silt strider service is available at the south edge of the Foreign Quarter, traveling from Narsis to Hlerynhul, Andrethis and Ald Horak. A guar cart near the Canyon Keep in the Market Quarter travels to Shipal-Sharai and Stormgate Pass. Ships from the docks at the Foreign Quarter travel to Hlerynhul, Sadrathim, and Othmura, and low-fare gondolas shuttle passengers around the city and outskirts via the Thirr river.<br>

|Name|    Guide to Necrom [T_Sc_GuideToNecrom]
|Model|    m\Text_Scroll_01.NIF
|Weight|    0.20
|Value|    3
|Scroll|    True
|Enchantment|    0
|Icon|    m\tx_scroll_01.dds
|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Necrom<br> <br>
<IMG SRC="TR\necrom_map_color.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="253"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Necrom is the Holy City of the Dead located on the easternmost part of mainland Morrowind in the Sacred Lands region. This Temple city is where the Dunmer dead are brought, and it's one of the most important pilgrimage sites in Morrowind. The name Necrom actually refers to the vast and ancient catacombs under the city, which is why the city often called the "city above Necrom" to distinguish it from the "city below". There are four distinct areas to the city above: the Waterfront, the Charnelworks, the Upper District and the Temple District. The Empire has no presence in Necrom and outlanders should be warned. Both the city above and the catacombs are guarded by the Ordinators in Mourning, an elite cadre of their order, who will protect the silence of Necrom against anyone who would dare to disturb it. Weapons, spells, or any disrespectful behavior are forbidden in the Holy City under the penalty of death. <br> <br>
The Waterfront <br> <br>
The Waterfront is where the docks are located and it's through here where most outlanders who visit Necrom enter the city. A trader and a hostel provide their services to travellers who are just passing by, while the city proper is accessed through the large docks administration building.
<br> <br>
The Charnelworks <br> <br>
The Charnelworks is the lower quarter of the city above Necrom and a place of great mourning. The dead are brought here in through the Pilgrim's Gate for preparation before they're taken to the catacombs. The district is the home of the priests and workers who help prepare and cremate the bodies, and it is also where the Temple bone-smiths create the holy guardians known as bonewalkers in their smithies. The catacombs can be entered from the eastern side of the district. 
<br> <br>
The Upper District <br> <br>
In the Upper District a myriad of shrines and memorials of bygone days can be found as well as various services for pilgrims. A great number of Temple relics are kept here. Prominent pilgrimage sites include the Shrine of the First Citizens where the ancestors of today's Dunmer laid the foundations of the city and the Memorial to the War of the First Council. Outlanders should be reminded that these sites are not museums but places of worship and mourning. The Sinner's Gate, known thusly for being used by pilgrims who try to keep their distance from their dead ancestors, is located in the southeastern corner of the district.
<br> <br>
The Temple District <br> <br>
The Temple district is dominated by the mighty Fane of the Ancestors which stands atop the large Temple complex. Inside the Fane are shrines devoted to the Tribunal gods Almalexia, Vivec and Sotha Sil and their Anticipations the Daedra Princes Boethiah, Mephala and Azura. Strong ancestral magics flow through the Fane powering the Ghostfence on Vvardenfell. Underneath the Fane are the forbidden Temple vaults of Necrom.
<br> <br>
The Catacombs <br> <br>
Mourners and pilgrims can access the Catacombs from the Charnelworks district. It is here where the true City of the Dead lies. The lower reaches of the catacombs date back to the arrival of the Velothi in Morrowind. The catacombs are far too large and complex to map, and they are ever expanded to make room for new generations of dead. The ancient spirits guard their resting place with great passion, but they will also whisper their secrets to pilgrims if they have the ears to listen.
<br> <br>
Notable figures <br> <br>
Her eminence the Archmatron, Alvu Sareleth, can be found in the High Offices in the Temple district. Marshal Verendas Hlervan and Canon Simine Turethi, who are in command of the Ordinators in Mourning, can be found in the Watch Barracks in the Upper District and the Hall of Contemplation in the Temple district, respectively. Bradys Hlaalo, in the Chamber of Parting, is the priest in charge of the mourning rituals and corpse preparation in the Charnelworks. Ethaso Athones is in charge of the docks administration in the Waterfront.
<br> <br>
Transportation <br> <br>
Ship transport to and from Necrom can be found in the settlements of Enamor Dayn and Alt Bosara. The Silt Strider takes passengers to Sailen and Akamora. <br>

|Name|    Guide to Old Ebonheart [T_Sc_GuideToOldEbonheartTR]
|Model|    M\text_scroll_01.nif
|Weight|    0.20
|Value|    3
|Scroll|    True
|Enchantment|    0
|Icon|    m\tx_scroll_01.dds
|Text|    <DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="3" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Guide to Old Ebonheart<br> <br>
<IMG SRC="TR\oldebonheart_city_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Old Ebonheart is the beating heart of the Empire in Morrowind and the largest Imperial city in all the East. Seated at the very mouth of the mighty Thirr River, the city is a mighty symbol of Imperial culture and military power, and a friendly haven for travelers in the often-hostile lands of the Dark Elves.

Despite its mainland location, Old Ebonheart is part of Vvardenfell District, and the legal seat of its Duke, the noble Vedam Dren. Duke Dren, having relocated his administration to the new Ebonheart-upon-Vvardenfell in the Ascadian Isles, has left governance of the city in the hands of Burgrave Caros Cocceius, Castellan of the Ebon Tower.

Travelers entering Old Ebonheart will pass beneath a striking statue of Talos, watching over his great eastern city just as he did in life. Newcomers are required to declare any proscribed or taxable goods at the Census Office found here. The main road north continues further into Old Ebonheart, dividing the city proper into two halves. Off this main thoroughfare, a civilian visitor can find the Moth and Tiger Inn and the Guild of Mages, while weary Legionnaires may rest their heads at the Legion Boarding House.

Old Ebonheart is a city of astonishing delights, but none are more beautiful than the Grand Chapel of Talos, known across the Empire for its fine glasswork and stolid, yet beautiful architecture. Old Ebonheart's west side, where the Grand Chapel can be found, is built around the historic Fountain Plaza, where many of the city's oldest and most prominent institutions are located. The grand guild hall of the Guild of Fighters is on the Plaza, as are the Morrowind headquarters of the Briricca Private Bank and the East Empire Company. The esteemed Imperial Archaeological Society also has its Morrowind headquarters here; its museum - open to visitors - is the finest public collection of Dark Elven and Dwarven antiquities anywhere in Tamriel.

The eastern city is the dense core of Old Ebonheart's economic might. In its tight alleyways and busy shops, an enterprising buyer can find goods and services of a thousand varieties, while the docks service traders from across the Empire. Two inns in the eastern city provide lodgings - the Empress Katariah and the Salty Futtocks - though the editors of the Guide recommend that visitors avoid the latter, a tavern of low repute. The Hostel of Stendarr's Mercy may also provide for travelers seeking charitable accommodations.

<br> <br>
<IMG SRC="TR\oldebonheart_ebontower_city_map.dds" WIDTH="377" HEIGHT="377"><br><br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">

Across the bridge from the Fountain Plaza, the Ebon Tower complex is an immense testament to Imperial architecture and fortification design. Eight towers, each named for a Divine, guard the spiraling double walls of the fortress, crowned by Talos' Tower - the tallest structure in the Eastern Provinces. Besides the Ebon Tower itself, the fortress courtyard hosts the headquarters of the Imperial Legion in Morrowind, as well as the Hall of Justice, seat of the Imperial Curia in Morrowind. Citizens wishing to arrange for permanent residence in Morrowind may inquire at the Resettlement Office, while those seeking the resources of a Provincial Mission may find them here. Travelers from Skyrim and Black Marsh should note, however, that those Provinces' Missions have been relocated to Ebonheart-on-Vvardenfell.

<DIV ALIGN="CENTER"><FONT COLOR="000000" SIZE="2" FACE="Magic Cards"><br>
Region Information
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT">
Old Ebonheart is in the Aanthirin region, the fertile hills that surround the lower Thirr River. Vvardenfell District ends at the city's walls; the rest of the region is a part of Mournhold District. To the south, the villages of Dondril and Felms Ithul are only a short trek from Old Ebonheart's gates, while the Dark Elf Temple outpost of Serynthul can be found to the east. Further south, the larger town of Vhul is one of the more notable sources of the closely-guarded native drink called punavit.

All three of the aforementioned Dark Elf settlements are ruled by the enigmatic lord of Roa Dyr, a chapel-fortress of the local Great House Indoril. Roa Dyr does not exclude visitors, but travelers are urged to take care not to offend the often-prickly Indoril. There are few services in Roa Dyr available to travelers, and no inn.

Across the river, on the western banks, a smattering of rich plantations form the eastern border of House Hlaalu territory. While members of the Hlaalu are friendlier to western travelers than their Indoril counterparts, visitors - particularly natives of Black Marsh and Elsweyr - are advised to remain alert, as it is on these plantations that the most savage customs of the Dark Elves are maintained. Should travelers find themselves embroiled in a dispute, the Guild of Barristers chapter in Old Ebonheart often handles complex issues of local and Imperial law.

The road south from Old Ebonheart terminates at its confluence with the great Veloth's Path. a well-maintained road sacred to the Dark Elves. From here, a traveler may proceed east to Mournhold, or west across the bridge-city of Almas Thirr towards the Narsis and Velothis Districts.

There are several ruined Daedric, Dwarven, and Dark Elf complexes in and around the Aanthirin. Despite the docile and civilized nature of the Aanthirin, many of these ruins are extremely dangerous. Travelers should take care to avoid the Dwarf ruins of Bthung (east of Old Ebonheart) and Bthungtch (southwest of Almas Thirr), as well as the very prominent Daedric temple of Hadrumnibibi on an island directly south of Old Ebonheart. Most dangerous of all is the abandoned Indoril citadel of Tur Julan, found on the cliffs above the Hlaalu plantations on the western bank of the Thirr. It is said that these ruins are inhabited permanently by powerful Daedric guardians, who do not hesitate to slaughter unwary visitors.

If the reader has business on Vvardenfell, the modest new fortress of Ebonheart on the island is a recommended port of entry. Though services are much more limited than its mainland counterpart, the Six Fishes Inn provides beds, and there is easy access to Vivec City. Before traveling around Vvardenfell, however, those who have not already registered with the Census and Excise Office in Old Ebonheart, should first detour to the small village of Seyda Neen, where the only Census office on the Black Isle can be found.

<br>
Ode to a Prince's Wealth<br>
<br>
<DIV ALIGN="LEFT"><br>
Merchant prince of pious Niben stock
Tell us how your handsome wealth is made
Is it in the sacred house of silk?
Is it overseas on ships of trade?
Perhaps where ruby riches are unearthed
Or where men are parted from their drakes
Golden brothels, gilded dens of mirth
Home to courtesans and sotted rakes
<br>

Gambling houses, honest and less-so
Surely line your pockets, regal sire
As do breweries, where liquor flows
Industry whose profits never tire
Or is fishing where your interests lie?
River's bounty worth its weight in gold
Money too, in abattoir's supply
Is it beef whose treasure fills your hold?
<br>

In the city, wealth is toilsome made
Stench of sload oil makes the stomach turn
Hammers clang till hearing starts to fade
Magic mixtures make the nostrils burn
Workshops toil unceasing, day and night
Kilns and dyers breathe a foulsome smell
Renter's meager pay is your delight
Debtors 'neath your looming shadow dwell
<br>

Is your wealth a gift from the divine?
Or is it merely humble man's design?
<br>
